facts.fact: 闹鬼之地是卢顿酒店（Luton Hotel），叙述者对它最熟悉；如今只剩倾斜的残壳，楼址下面是一个大坑。
facts.anchor: the one I know best is the Luton Hotel. The shell of the old hotel leans like a forlorn lover.

facts.fact: Redbird 叔叔抱怨酒店“给好色之徒的房间多于给病人的”：医院只有 20 张床，Luton 却有 35 张。
facts.anchor: “More rooms for the lecherous than for the sickly,” Uncle Redbird would grumble. The hospital had only twenty beds; the Luton, thirty-five.

facts.fact: 三层高的酒店白色护墙板楼身坐在石块加灰浆的地基上，Redbird 把这些石头叫作 Slave rocks（奴隶石）。
facts.anchor: Three stories high, the hotel’s white clapboard torso sat on a stone and mortar foundation. Slave rocks, Redbird called them.

facts.fact: 传闻酒店主雇流浪汉采石：5 个人开工，到发薪日只剩 3 人。
facts.anchor: Five men started the job, only three remained on payday.

facts.fact: 石头离开原生之地后会哭泣；起初它造成的积水被归咎于排水不良。
facts.anchor: Away from their natural home, the rocks wept. At first, the flooding they caused was attributed to poor drainage.

facts.fact: 祖父石（the Grandfathers）最终烧毁了酒店；许多人怀疑是 Redbird，或叙述者“我”——两人互为不在场证明。
facts.anchor: THE GRANDFATHERS BURNED the building finally. I know many think it was Redbird. Or me. Because I was his alibi and he mine.

facts.fact: Redbird 已去世，给“我”留下他的河畔小屋、汗屋和工具，撬棍还在等待。
facts.anchor: Redbird is gone. He left me his river shack, his sweat lodge, his tools. The crowbar waits.

facts.fact: 结尾叙述者用长满老茧的手指数“所有被移走之物”（all of the removals）。
facts.anchor: On my calloused fingers I count all of the removals.
